subject: Post-call recap & test plan: BlueForge perf discovery
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@blueforge.com>, Aria Patel <aria@blueforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & test plan: BlueForge perf discovery

Thanks again for the time this morning — good to connect. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the bench run: 

Summary of call:
- Goal: quantify latency (p95/p99) and steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) for your typical customer flows vs your current hyperscaler provider and Redwood hosted endpoints.
- Workloads discussed: short chat prompts (~32 tokens), medium Q&A (~128 tokens), long summarization (~512 tokens).
- Key success metrics: p95 < 150ms for short prompts, p99 within 2x p95, sustained tokens/sec to support 200 RPS baseline for medium workloads.

Action items (proposed):
1) BlueForge to confirm which two representative prompt sets we should run — sending a sample prompt CSV attached (sample-prompt-set.csv).
2) Redwood to stand up a bench harness that runs A/B tests against: (A) your current hyperscaler endpoint (we'll mirror their request pattern), (B) Redwood hosted endpoint (model X-3 quantized/optimized).
3) Define measurement windows: 10-minute warmup, 30-minute steady-state; capture p50/p90/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec.
4) Provide access details for the hyperscaler test account and any request throttles.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: confirm prompt set + hyperscaler credentials (Andrew).
- Tomorrow: Redwood prepares bench configs and shares benchmark-config.yaml (attached).
- Day after: run baseline A/B, share preliminary p95/p99 + tokens/sec heatmap.

Benchnotes / configuration highlights (attached): benchmark-config.yaml contains the test matrix. Key defaults: concurrency sweep [8, 16, 32], sequence lengths [32, 128, 512], batching window 8ms, KV-cache pre-warmed for long-context tests, int8 quant model variant for Redwood.

Questions for you now:
- Is the 200 RPS baseline still representative for your production (you mentioned spikes to ~800 during business hours)?
- Any IP/network restrictions on the hyperscaler side (we'll need an IP allowlist or a test token)?

I've attached the initial bench config and a small prompt sample. If that looks right I'll slot the run for Friday morning PST and loop in Marissa to own execution.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Attachments: benchmark-config.yaml (text), sample-prompt-set.csv (csv)
From: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@blueforge.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Aria Patel <aria@blueforge.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & test plan: BlueForge perf discovery

Thanks Nikhil — this is great and aligned with what we discussed. Quick answers: 
- The three prompt lengths look good. We'll add two customer prompts to the CSV (one short chat, one long doc-summary).
- Baseline RPS: 200 steady, spikes to 800 for 2-3 minute bursts during ingest windows.
- We'll send a test API key for our hyperscaler endpoint and a public source of truth for their rate limits by EOD.

Please prioritize p99 capture and include tail latency plots — those are what our infra team cares about. Also include measured CPU/GPU utilization if possible.

I'll expect the preliminary results Friday. Thanks — Andrew

Andrew Cho
Lead Platform Engineer, BlueForge
andrew.cho@blueforge.com
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@blueforge.com>, Aria Patel <aria@blueforge.com>
Date: 2028-08-10T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: BlueForge bench matrix + owner assign (please review)

Marissa / Priyom — moving this to the internal thread so we can lock down the matrix before running. Copying the external team for transparency. 

Planned test matrix (proposed):
- Endpoints: (1) BlueForge current hyperscaler (their API) (2) Redwood hosted (model: redwood-x-3-int8) (3) Redwood fallback variant (redwood-x-3-fp16) for comparison.
- Sequence lengths: 32 / 128 / 512 tokens.
- Concurrency sweep: 8, 16, 32, 64.
- Windows: 10m warmup, 30m steady-state (collect per-second metrics).
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, error rate, GPU util, memory headroom, median KV cache hit-rate (for long context).

A/B plan specifics:
- Run Hyperscaler vs Redwood each with identical traffic generator (same seed/randomization).
- Use batching: Redwood default batching window 8ms; hyperscaler equivalent TBD (we'll document).
- Tokenization: use our tokenizer to normalize token counts; report both model-token/sec and user-token/sec.

Targets and pass/fail guidance (for discussion with BlueForge):
- Short prompts (32 tokens): target p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms.
- Medium (128 tokens): p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms.
- Throughput: achieve >= tokens/sec required for 200 RPS steady + 3x burst headroom.

Operational responsibilities:
- Marissa: own run execution + results deck + tail-latency plots.
- Priyom: instrument tracing/metrics export and normalize hyperscaler telemetry to our schema.
- Nikhil: coordinate with BlueForge for hyperscaler creds, procurement hooks, and scheduling.

Attachments: benchmark-config.yaml (edited), will add the final prompt CSV once BlueForge confirms.

Priyom — please validate the batching/window settings in the config and add a stanza for quantized model parity checks (int8 vs fp16) so we can comment on quality delta (latency vs perplexity).

Thanks,
Nikhil
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@blueforge.com>
Date: 2028-08-10T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: BlueForge bench matrix + owner assign (please review)

Adding a couple of clarifications from the ops perspective: 
1) Hyperscaler parity: we need an exact list of flags the hyperscaler is using (beam size, streaming vs non-streaming, token flush policy). If they stream, tail behavior will differ and we should capture both.
2) Cost estimates: I'll put together a quick cost-per-1M-token delta for Redwood-hosted vs hyperscaler (draft attached: cost-estimate.xlsx). This will be helpful for commercial discussions.
3) Schedule: Friday morning is tight for us; can we target Monday 08/13 for the run? That gives time to validate tokenization parity and get a clean 30-minute steady-state.

Forwarding the bench matrix to Priyom — please ensure we instrument p99 with percentile bucketing at 10ms granularity. Also we should capture per-shard GPU util (Nvidia SMI snapshots) every 30s.

On trace/observability, include a short link to Redwood Console run: https://redwood.app/s/drive/blueforge-bench-202808 (I'll add results folder post-run).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: cost-estimate.xlsx

All — thanks for the clarity and the updated plan. Monday 08/13 works for our side. A few notes before the run: 
- We've provisioned a temporary test key for our hyperscaler account and attached an allowlist entry for Redwood's bench IPs. Credentials will be uploaded to the secure link in the next message.
- Procurement: our procurement team requires that any sustained p99 > 2s be escalated as a potential SLA risk; we understand this and will treat it as informational for now.
- Can you include a short section in the results that maps latency improvements to customer cost savings (helpful for our CFO).

We'll be available during the run and can share logs if anything unexpected pops up. Looking forward to the comparison.

Best,
Andrew
